newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stora sees less investment after Q1 1998.
newsitem.headline: Stora sees less investment after Q1 1998.

text.p: Swedish forestry group Stora AB said on Monday it will have finalised the main part of its investment programme in the first quarter of 1998.

Thereafter, investment costs will fall by a few billion crowns annually, which will have a positive effect on cash flow and earnings, the company's chief executive Lars-Ake Helgesson said in Stora's annual report.
"To say that Stora thereafter will be fully invested for a number of years would be an exaggeration, but we don't see any further new investments in the foreseeable future," he said.
"Now continued capital efficiency but also growth will be in focus," he said.
Helgesson was cautious but optimistic regarding 1997.
"During 1997 we expect an improved economic development in Europe," he said.
"We also expect prices for most of our product areas will turn upwards in 1997 trendwise, but it is not a given that average prices in 1997 will be at a higher level than in 1996."
